::: {.callout-important}
## Module 3 is required
[Module 3](module3.qmd) is a prerequisite. This session is hands-on project work,
not instruction, and it assumes you can already choose and run an appropriate
statistical test.
:::

The home stretch. A session for the intermediate R user to practise
**end-to-end data analysis** — in small groups, on a question you bring.

We use `data/data.RDS` — a synthetic dataset organised the same way as the main
ABCD dataset, described in full on the [dataset reference page](data.qmd) — to ask
basic scientific questions. In your group you will:

- build a hypothesis
- decide on the appropriate statistical test
- use R to run the analysis and produce the visualisations

The goal is to leave with a **proto-poster** — a first draft of the kind of results
you would put on a scientific poster at a conference. Here is the shape to aim for:

[Download an example poster (.pptx)](../scripts/module3/Poster_Example.pptx){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}

## Before the session

A few things to line up beforehand so your group can hit the ground running on
Nov 12:

- **By Nov 4** — let Andrew and Billu know whether you are attending Module 4, so
  no one is left without a group for the final projects.
- **Nov 4–11** — work with your group, over email or Zoom, to agree on a question
  you can turn into a poster.
- **By Nov 11** — send Andrew and Billu your proposed research question along with
  its **dependent and independent variables**. You can change these later, but
  have something lined up before the session.
- **Review Modules 0–3** — you will need these skills to build your poster.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Lining up your question
- Download [the dataset and its dictionaries](data.qmd#get-the-files) into your
  project's `data/` folder.
- Browse the [variable list](data.qmd#browse-the-variables) — your question has to
  be answerable from these 53 columns.
- Reuse a [Module 3 template](module3.qmd#before-you-start) that fits the shape of
  your question. Don't have a question? We supply them.
:::

## During the session · Nov 12

We will use the whole time to practise what we have learned, working in our small
groups so you can troubleshoot and manipulate code together. This is the
culmination of — and the reason for — the whole workshop, so engage with your
group mates: science is a team sport, and this is the chance to practise it.

Groups will also present their code and their poster draft to the room. That is
just so we can troubleshoot together as a big group, and show off how far everyone
has come.
